nodes.label: Idempotent Auto-Subscribe Free Plan
nodes.rationale: Automatically provisioning the free tier after OAuth improves onboarding; failures are logged but do not block login, and the operation is idempotent and feature-flagged.

nodes.label: Subscription Ownership Assertion
nodes.rationale: Checking a requested subscription ID against the authenticated user’s own subscription list and returning 404 prevents cross-user IDOR access without revealing whether another user’s ID exists.
nodes.source_location: ### 5.4 Task 1.3: Buat Modul Subscriptions (Proxy ke Payment-Service)

nodes.label: POS Production Blueprint Adoption
nodes.rationale: The POS implementation is adopted because its ownership assertions, error handling, logging, and data model are production-tested, and payment-service endpoints follow that contract.

nodes.label: Public Website Subscription Paywall
nodes.rationale: An inactive paid subscription should make the public renderer show an inactive-site notice rather than serve the normal website; payment-service lookup failures are treated defensively as active to avoid taking down a site.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Subscription and Wallet Architecture
nodes.rationale: The admin frontend acts as a BFF, the Website API owns authenticated user-facing routes, and the payment service remains the core engine for subscriptions, wallets, billing, and recurring charges.

nodes.label: Default Free Plan Limits
nodes.rationale: Users without a subscription receive conservative FREE defaults, preventing unmetered resource creation before subscription.

nodes.label: Local Subscription Cache for Plan-Limit Enforcement
nodes.norm_label: local subscription cache for plan-limit enforcement
nodes.rationale: Local TypeORM entities cache authoritative payment-service subscription data so plan limits can be enforced without a network call; payment-service remains the source of truth.
nodes.source_location: ### 5.2 Task 1.1: Buat Entity TypeORM untuk Table Subscription

nodes.label: Supabase Migration Schema Management
nodes.rationale: Database schema is managed through Supabase migrations rather than TypeORM synchronize, avoiding runtime schema ownership by the ORM.

nodes.label: TypeORM Query Layer
nodes.rationale: TypeORM is used for queries only; migrations remain the source of database schema changes.

nodes.label: JWT-Derived User Identity
nodes.rationale: Mutating and querying wallet/subscription routes must derive userId from the authenticated JWT via @CurrentUser(), never from client-supplied body or parameters.

nodes.label: Per-User Wallet and Subscription Ownership
nodes.rationale: One user owns one IDR wallet and one active subscription across all their websites; this keeps MVP billing simple and follows the proven POS pattern while leaving room for later per-website scope.

nodes.label: Invitation Link Expiry and Recipient Restriction
nodes.norm_label: invitation link expiry and recipient restriction
nodes.rationale: The invitation URL has an expiry and is intended only for the invitee, so it should not be forwarded.

nodes.label: Private Invitation Email Delivery
nodes.rationale: Email is sent for private invitations with an email address; WhatsApp-only invitations are shared manually from the invitation manager.

nodes.label: Escrow Checkout for Gathering Invoices
nodes.rationale: Payment funds are held through escrow and returned to the paying wallet if a refund is needed; the initiator can pay multiple invoices in one checkout.

nodes.label: Invoice Order-Link Fallback
nodes.rationale: Before checkout the order link points to invoice details; after a checkout transaction exists it opens the transaction order detail.

nodes.label: Public-Safe Invoice Summary with Authenticated Payment
nodes.norm_label: public-safe invoice summary with authenticated payment
nodes.rationale: Invoice links expose only a public-safe summary; payment still requires login using the reservation email account.

nodes.label: Email OTP Verification for Public RSVP
nodes.norm_label: email otp verification for public rsvp
nodes.rationale: A registration is created only after the attendee successfully verifies the one-time code; the code is single-use and email-only until WhatsApp OTP integration exists.

nodes.label: Batch RSVP Rejection Eligibility
nodes.rationale: Batch rejection is limited to active unpaid RSVP reservations that do not have a seat order.

nodes.label: Retained Rejected Registration History
nodes.rationale: Rejection does not erase registration history: status, organizer message, and rejection time are stored with the registration record.
